title: Blink: the first program on a microcontroller
instructions:
## Hello, world with an LED

An LED is wired to pin 13 of the board (the one with the built-in LED). Make it blink **once a second**: on for 500 ms, off for 500 ms.

## Do this

1. In `setup()`, set pin 13 as an output with `pinMode`.
2. In `loop()`, switch it on with `digitalWrite(13, HIGH)`, wait with `delay(500)`, switch it off, wait again.
3. Press **Upload and run** and read the pin timeline. The simulator runs five seconds of board time.
hints: pinMode(13, OUTPUT); goes in setup(), which runs once.
loop() runs again and again: digitalWrite(13, HIGH); delay(500); digitalWrite(13, LOW); delay(500);
Without a delay the LED toggles thousands of times a second and looks dimly on.

checks.label: Pin 13 is configured as an output
The LED blinks with a 1 s period

realityNote: On a real Uno the sketch is compiled by avr-gcc and flashed over USB; the built-in LED is on pin 13 through a small resistor. delay() blocks everything, which is why later labs replace it with millis().
